Bethul
BETH-ul
proper noun
A city in the inheritance of the tribe of Simeon, within the territory of Judah; called Bethuel by the Chronicler and Chesil in the parallel Judah list. The name is taken to mean “dweller in God” or “man of God.”

📖 Biblical Definition

Bethul is a city given to the tribe of Simeon, whose portion lay within the borders of Judah in the dry south country: “And Eltolad, and Bethul, and Hormah” (Jos 19:4). The Chronicler names the same town Bethuel (1Ch 4:30), and it appears as Chesil in the parallel Judah list (Jos 15:30). The name is taken to mean dweller in God, or man of God. This is fitting for a town of Simeon, for Simeon had no separate country but dwelt scattered in the midst of Judah, his inheritance swallowed up in his brother’s — a living fulfilment of Jacob’s dying word: “I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Israel” (Gen 49:7). What was spoken over Simeon and Levi as a chastening for their fierce anger became, in Levi’s case, a means of blessing, as the priests were scattered to teach; and Simeon too was preserved, not blotted out, dwelling among his brethren. A town called “dweller in God” set in this scattered inheritance quietly preaches that the true dwelling-place of God’s people is not a plot of ground but the LORD Himself: “Lord, thou hast been our dwelling place in all generations” (Psa 90:1). Simeon’s scattering could not rob him of the only home that finally matters — the God who is Himself the habitation of His people.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A city of Simeon within Judah’s borders, called Bethuel and Chesil elsewhere; the name means “dweller in God.”

BETHUL, a city in the inheritance of Simeon, within the territory of Judah.

It is called Bethuel by the Chronicler and Chesil in the parallel Judah list.

The name is taken to mean dweller in God, or man of God.

Simeon had no separate country but dwelt scattered among Judah.

The name witnesses that God Himself is the dwelling-place of His people.

📖 Key Scripture

Jos 19:4 — "And Eltolad, and Bethul, and Hormah,"

1Ch 4:30 — "And at Bethuel, and at Hormah, and at Ziklag,"

Gen 49:7 — "Cursed be their anger, for it was fierce; and their wrath, for it was cruel: I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Israel."

Psa 90:1 — "A Prayer of Moses the man of God. Lord, thou hast been our dwelling place in all generations."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A city of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it recovers the truth that the LORD Himself, not any plot of ground, is the abiding dwelling-place of His people.

expand to see more

Bethul faces no postmodern redefinition. The truth its name carries answers the restless heart that seeks its security and home in place, possession, and circumstance, forgetting that these are all passing and cannot finally house the soul.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that God is His people’s dwelling-place. Scattered Simeon, with a town named ‘dweller in God,’ teaches that the saints’ true home is not a country but the LORD, who has been our dwelling place in all generations.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

A city of Simeon within Judah, called Bethuel and Chesil; the name means “dweller in God,” witnessing that God is His people’s home.

Bethul — a city of Simeon within Judah’s borders (Jos 19:4).

It is called Bethuel by the Chronicler (1Ch 4:30) and Chesil elsewhere.

The name is taken to mean dweller in God, or man of God.

"Scattered Simeon dwelt in towns like Bethul, in the midst of Judah."
